releases.name: Switchboard 0.3.1
releases.body:
Switchboard now takes part in Passport group threads. Post once to an approved group and every other member receives it; reply to a received group message and the reply reaches the whole thread.

- `switchboard message send --group <group_id> "..."` posts to the group's thread. `--reply-to <local_message_id>` on a received group copy answers the whole thread with no recipient. `--conversation <thread_id>` continues a thread this store already knows. `--from <client_id>` selects the sending installation for owner posts.
- The same options reach `message-send --json`, the Claude Code channel tool, and the OpenCode tool, where `to` is now optional. `passport_message_status` also accepts a `post_id` for posts the calling client sent.
- Receipts and inbox rows carry `conversation_kind` and `hosted_post_id`. Group envelopes are marked `kind="group"` and tell the agent that a reply reaches every member. Pair envelopes are unchanged.
- A thread at its post cap returns `conversation_capped`. Switchboard stops retrying, keeps the thread id on the receipt, and points at `switchboard message propose --kind continue --conversation-id <id>`. Other send failures Passport marks as not retryable also expire at once instead of retrying for a day.
- Registration is cached per client and link, so discovery no longer re-registers every paired client on every send and stays clear of Passport's register throttle. Group sends get a 30 second timeout for fan-out uploads.
- `message agents` labels each hosted agent's presence: live through events, reachable through a wake webhook, or offline.
- The store migrates forward to schema 12 on first open. Back up `~/.switchboard` first, as DOCS.md describes.

Install or upgrade with `npm install --global @egoistmachines/switchboard` and rerun `switchboard coding install`. The OpenCode plugin is 0.1.4.

releases.name: Switchboard 0.3.0
releases.body:
Switchboard now carries messages between your agents. Paired editors on one machine message each other with no account and no network. A linked store also reaches your hosted agents through Passport, using the device credential it already has.

- Local messages between paired clients: `switchboard message send --to <client_id> "..."`, `message list`, `message agents`, and `config messaging on|off`. Bodies are screened and stored in the existing content store; receipts are content free.
- Delivery into every coding host. Claude Code gets a channel MCP server installed by `switchboard coding install` (start Claude with `--dangerously-load-development-channels server:switchboard` while channels are in research preview). OpenCode's plugin pushes into the active session. Codex and Cursor receive at the next prompt through the existing hook.
- Hosted messaging through the link you already have. One relay per store registers your paired editors on Passport, receives pushes, pulls hosted messages into the local inbox, and forwards local sends with idempotent retries.
- Agents propose collaborations. `message agents` lists every hosted agent of the owner. A send to a peer without a shared group carries `--purpose` and stays held until you approve it in the Passport Inbox on web or iOS, with a push notification. `message propose` asks explicitly, including renewals and continuations.
- The store migrates forward to schema 11 on first open. Back up `~/.switchboard` first, as DOCS.md describes.

Install with `npm install --global @egoistmachines/switchboard` and run `switchboard coding install`. The OpenCode plugin is 0.1.3.

releases.name: Switchboard 0.2.3
releases.body:
The published package now includes the Cursor adapter, which landed in the repository after 0.2.2 shipped. Install with `npm install --global @egoistmachines/switchboard` and run `switchboard coding install` to pair Cursor alongside OpenCode, Claude Code, and Codex.

The README opens with a recorded demo, a zero-install `npx` try-it block, and a plain statement that local use needs no account and makes no network calls. `switchboard init` no longer describes the local store as "your AI Passport". SECURITY.md documents the reporting route and what leaves the machine during linking and sync, and CHANGELOG.md covers every release from 0.1.0. The `mcp` npm keyword is gone, since this package ships no MCP server.

The OpenCode plugin is unchanged at 0.1.2.

releases.name: Switchboard 0.2.2
releases.body:
Sync client hardening: the client now tolerates the hosted upload wire's retryable and truncated outcomes, ends cycles ok with pending work, adopts the server cursor after a lost ack when every gap change is already recorded locally, retries the idempotent ack once, and reports six distinct failure statuses instead of one generic line. Terminal content rejections surface per item with category and creation time, and coding import screens candidates before the prompt.

OpenCode now installs globally by default so the adapter follows the owner into every project, with a per-project option via --project. Installs and uninstalls into a shared node_modules are gated on npm's own tracking manifest so nothing user-owned is ever deleted, and uninstall removes everything the installer created.

CONTRIBUTING documents the disposable end-to-end testing posture with a helper script.

The OpenCode plugin is unchanged at 0.1.2.

releases.name: Switchboard 0.2.1
releases.body:
Switchboard 0.2.1 moves the OpenCode plugin into this repository and republishes both packages with scrubbed public documentation.

- The plugin ships from packages/opencode-switchboard as @egoistmachines/opencode-switchboard@0.1.2 and the installer pins that version.
- The publish workflow releases both packages with provenance from CI.
- The switchboard suite exercises the plugin seam in-repo, including framing parity and a packed-plugin install.

Upgrade with: npm install --global @egoistmachines/switchboard
